paper.title: Adversarially Robust Multi-Armed Bandit Algorithm with Variance-Dependent Regret Bounds

settings.definition_quote: In a stochastic setting, $\ell(t) $ follows an unknown distribution $\cD$ over $[0, 1]^K$, i.i.d.~for $t = 1, 2, \ldots, T$.

In the adversarial setting, we do not assume any generative models for the loss vector $\ell(t)$, but it can be chosen in an adversarial manner. More precisely, in each round, $\ell(t)$ may depend on the history of loss vectors and chosen arms

unmapped: corruption level C = E[sum_t ||l'(t)-l(t)||_inf]; regret measured on corrupted losses
settings.definition_quote: a \textit{temporary loss} $\ell'(t) \in [0, 1]^K$ is generated from an unknown distribution $\cD$, and the adversary then corrupts $\ell'(t)$ to determine $\ell(t)$. We define the \textit{corruption level} $C \geq 0$ by $C = \E [ \sum_{t=1}^T \| \ell'(t) - \ell(t) \|_{\infty} ]$.

bound.expression_latex: R(T) \leq ( 2(1+\epsilon) + \sum_{i \neq i^*} \max\{4\frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} + c \log (1 + \frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i}), 2(1+\epsilon)\} ) \log T + o (\log T)
bound.regime: bound on limsup_{T->inf} R(T)/log T (theorem states leading term times log T plus o(log T))

symbols.c_alg: constant c = O((log(1/epsilon))^2) depending on the input parameter

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: In any stochastic setting with a unique optimal arm, the proposed algorithm achieves R(T) \leq ( 2 (1+\epsilon) + \sum_{i \in [K] \setminus \{ i^* \}} \max\{4\frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} + c \log ( 1 + \frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} ), 2(1+\epsilon)\} ) \log T + o (\log T), where ... $c = O((\log \frac{1}{\epsilon})^2)$.

results.notes: sigma_i^2 is the loss variance of arm i. Encoded as coefficient of log T (limsup of R/log T), equivalent to Proposition prop:bound-sto bound.

bound.regime: epsilon = 0.2; bound on limsup R(T)/log T

source.label: table:regretbound-sto
source.quote: in the case of $\epsilon = 0.2$, we can confirm numerically that $h(z) \leq \max\{ 4 z + 4.2 \log (1+z), 2.4 \}$, which leads to the regret bound described in Table~\ref{table:regretbound-sto}.

results.notes: Numerically verified specialization, not a formal theorem statement.

bound.expression_latex: R(T) \leq \sqrt{K \log T \min\{ T, 4L^*, 4 (T-L^*), 4 Q_{\infty} \}} + O(K \log T)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: in adversarial settings, the regret for the proposed algorithm satisfies R(T) \leq \sqrt{K \log T \min\{ T, 4L^*,  4 (T-L^*),  4 Q_{\infty}  \}} + O(K \log T)

results.notes: Leading term has exact constant 1; O applies to K log T term only. L* = min_i E[sum_t l_i(t)].

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: R(T) \leq \sqrt{K \log T \min\{ T, 4L^*,  4 (T-L^*),  4 Q_{\infty}  \}} + O(K \log T)

results.notes: Worst-case specialization (min <= T) of the adversarial bound.

symbols.R_sto: RHS of stochastic bound: (2(1+eps_alg) + sum_subopt(Max(4*sigma_i**2/Delta_i + c_alg*log(1+sigma_i**2/Delta_i), 2(1+eps_alg))))*log(T) + o(log T)

source.label: prop:bound-corrupted
source.quote: In any corrupted stochastic setting with a unique optimal arm, the proposed algorithm achieves R(T) \leq \mathcal{R} + O(\sqrt{C \mathcal{R}}), where $\mathcal{R}$ is the RHS of \eqref{eq:thm1-bound-sto} and $C$ is the corruption level

results.notes: O applies to sqrt(C R) term; leading R has constant 1.

bound.expression_latex: R(T) \leq \sqrt{ \frac{K}{1-2\eta} ( \min\{ T, 4 L^*, 4 (T - L^*), 4 Q_{\infty}, \frac{8}{\eta} V_1 \} + \frac{K}{\eta} ) \log T } + O(K \log T)

source.label: eq:bound-pathlength
source.quote: by modifying the algorithm in the way described in Appendix~\ref{sec:path-length}, we can obtain a regret bound of R(T) \leq \sqrt{ \frac{K}{1-2\eta} ( \min\{ T, 4 L^*, 4 (T - L^*), 4 Q_{\infty}, \frac{8}{\eta} V_1 \} + \frac{K}{\eta} ) \log T } + O(K \log T) in adversarial settings, where $\eta \in (0, 1 / 2 )$ is an input parameter.

results.notes: Stated in a Remark, derived in Appendix C.

symbols.R_sto: RHS of the stochastic bound in Theorem 1

source.quote: In corrupted stochastic settings, this modified algoirthm achieves a regret bound of R(T) \leq  \frac{1}{1-2\eta} \mathcal{R} + O ( \sqrt{ \frac{1}{1-2\eta} C \mathcal{R} } + K \sqrt{\frac{ \log T }{\eta (1-2\eta)}} )

results.notes: Remark statement; proof sketched only for C=0 case in Appendix C.

bound.regime: liminf of R(T)/log T; 0 <= mu* < mu_i <= 1, sigma_i^2 <= mu_i(1-mu_i)

extra_assumptions: exists a loss distribution on [0,1]^K with given means and variances (worst-case instance for given moments)

source.label: prop_moment
source.quote: For any $0\le \mu^*<\mu_i\le 1$ and $\sigma_i^2 \le \mu_i(1-\mu_i)$, there exists a loss distribution $\mathcal{D}$ over $[0,1]^K$ such that any consistent algorithm suffers \liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{R(T)}{\log T} \ge \sum_{i\neq i^*} \frac{\Delta_i}{...} and there exists an algorithm achieving this bound with equality for all $\mathcal{D}$.

results.notes: Simplification of Honda & Takemura (2012) Theorem 4; means are losses (mu_star = optimal mean loss). Achievability part not recorded separately.
